chunks: From him, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from al-Hakam ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, that he heard Abd Allah ibn Ata saying:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Arise and saddle two animals, a donkey and a mule.' So I saddled a donkey and a mule and presented the mule to him, and I thought it was more beloved to him. He said: 'Who ordered you to present this mule to me?' I said: 'I chose it for you.' He said: 'And did I order you to choose for me?' Then he said: 'The most beloved of mounts to me are donkeys.'

He said: So I presented the donkey to him and held the stirrup for him. He mounted and said: 'Praise be to Allah who guided us by Islam and taught us the Quran and bestowed upon us Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). Praise be to Allah who made this subservient to us, though we were not able to do so, and surely to our Lord we are returning. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.'

He traveled and I followed until we reached another place. I said to him: 'The prayer, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'This is the valley of ants, one cannot pray in it.' Until we reached another place. I said to him the same. He said: 'This land is salty, one cannot pray in it.'

He said: Until he descended by himself. He said to me: 'Have you prayed or are you praying your Tasbih?' I said: 'This is a prayer which the people of Iraq call Al-Zawal.' He said: 'Those who pray are the Shias of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and it is the prayer of the Returners.' So he prayed and I prayed.

Then I held the stirrup for him. Then he said what he had said at the beginning. Then he said: 'O Allah, curse the Murji'ah, for they are our enemies in the world and the Hereafter.' I said to him: 'What reminded you of the Murji'ah, may I be sacrificed for you?' He said: 'They crossed my mind.'

key_terms.الرِّكَاب: Stirrup (used here to signify holding the mount for the Imam)
key_terms.الزَّوَالَ: Al-Zawal (a specific prayer time or type of prayer, often associated with Tasbih)
key_terms.الْمُرْجِئَة: Murji'ah (a theological sect known for delaying judgment of sinners)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْأَوَّابِينَ: The prayer of the Returners (referring to the prayer of Ali or the Shias)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred mode of transport for the Imams and the ruling on the prayer of Zawal according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi illustrates Imam al-Baqir’s (as) practical adherence to the Sunnah of the Prophet while distinguishing Shia practices, such as the Zawal prayer, from those of other sects. It provides specific jurisprudential details on prayer conditions, like avoiding impure ground, and links the 'Zawal' prayer to the 'Awwabinun' (the Devout), reinforcing its theological significance in Shia tradition. The mention of the Murji'ah highlights early sectarian dynamics, positioning the Shias as the true followers of Ali (as) in contrast to those who deferred judgment on leadership issues.

en.hubeali: H 14865 – From him, from Ibn Fazzaal, from Anbasat Bin Hishaam, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Al-Hakam Bin Muhammad Bin Al-Qasim that he heard Abdullah Bin Ata’a saying that:

Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Arise, and saddle two animals, a donkey and a mule’. So I saddled a donkey and a mule and offered the mule to himasws as I opined that it was more beloved of the two to himasws. heasws said: ‘Who ordered you to offer to measws this mule?’ I said, ‘I chose it for youasws’. Heasws said: ‘And did Iasws order you to choose for measws?’ Then said: ‘The most preferable of the pack, to measws is the donkey’.

So I offered the donkey to himasws and grabbed the reins for himasws. Heasws climbed upon it and said; ‘Praise be to Allahazwj Who Guided usasws by Al-Islam, and Taught usasws the Quran, and Bestowed upon usasws by Muhammadsaww. Praise be to Allahazwj “[43:13] Who made this subservient to us and we were not able to do it [43:14] And surely to our Lord we must return”, and Praise be to Allahazwj the Lordazwj of the Worlds’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> went and I went (with him<sup>asws</sup>) until we reached another place. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Salat, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a valley of the ants, one cannot Pray here’, until we reached another place. I said to him<sup>asws</sup> similar to that. He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘This is a salty ground, one cannot Pray here’.

(The narrator) said, ‘Until he<sup>asws</sup> descended by himself<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Have you Prayed or done your Glorification (Tasbeeh)?’ I said, ‘This Salat which the people of Iraq have named it as Al-Zawwaal’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Those who perform the ‘Salat’, are the Shites of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and it is the Salat which often reaches Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> Prayed, and I Prayed.

Then I grabbed the reins for himasws, then heasws said what heasws had said at the beginning, then said: ‘Our Allahazwj! Curse the Murjiites[27], for they are ourasws enemies in the world and the Hereafter’. So I said to himasws: ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws, what made youasws to remember the Murjiites?’ Heasws said: ‘Iasws just thought about them’.
